final.memo:
Charlie and I view the current environment as an exceptional opportunity for the long-term investor. With the market decline exceeding 41% from the 1973 highs and the earnings yield on equities outstripping the long bond by over 5 percentage points, we are finding prices that offer a substantial margin of safety [D04]. The pessimism permeating the market—characterized by talk of depression and a flight to gold—has created a climate where Mr. Market is offering us wonderful businesses at prices far below their intrinsic value [D03], [D05].

We do not concern ourselves with forecasting the economy or timing the market bottom, as such exercises are futile [D01], [D07]. Instead, we focus on the durability of earning power. We are uninterested in complex businesses requiring technological foresight; rather, we are looking for simple, understandable franchises—such as newspapers or utilities—with pricing power and reliable returns on capital [D01]. We are moving to deploy our capital as rapidly as these opportunities permit, keeping our focus strictly on the underlying economics of the businesses we acquire rather than the path of the index [D01], [D07].
